title: KL-Time Replay: Function-Space Drift Monitoring for Continual Learning in LLMs

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to determine when to replay in continual learning. Paper [6] explicitly addresses this purpose, proposing a method to learn the timing of replay scheduling in continual learning scenarios. The abstract states: "we propose that continual learning systems should learn the time to learn and schedule which tasks to replay at different time steps," which is substantively equivalent to the contribution's purpose.

### Mechanism
The contribution's mechanism involves using KL divergence on an anchor set to replace parameter-space signals with function-space drift. Paper [24] discusses detecting drifts in data streams using KL divergence, specifically for data engineering applications. While the application differs, the mechanism of using KL divergence to measure drift is substantively equivalent. Additionally, paper [19] introduces KL divergence regularization in a control setting, which aligns with the use of KL divergence as a measure of drift. Both papers cover the mechanism at the primitive level.

### Evaluation
The contribution evaluates its method on a 5-task text classification benchmark. Paper [14] evaluates continual learning methods for text classification using benchmarks, and paper [5] assesses multilingual continual learning approaches for text classification. Both papers use text classification benchmarks for continual learning evaluation, which matches the evaluation design. The specific benchmark instance differs, but the design is covered.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of LLM continual learning. Paper [7] explicitly addresses continual learning for foundation models (FMs), which are a subset of LLMs. Paper [14] also focuses on continual learning for text classification, which is a relevant subdomain within LLM continual learning. Both papers cover the domain.

Paper [7] "Adaptive Memory Replay for Continual Learning" also addresses adaptive replay scheduling. Both cover the purpose of determining when/whether to replay in continual learning.

**MECHANISM: "锚点集上 KL 散度(function-space drift)替换 FOREVER 参数空间信号" (KL divergence on anchor set as function-space drift signal, replacing parameter-space signal)**

Paper [6] uses a learned scheduling policy but does not use KL divergence on an anchor set as a function-space drift signal. Paper [7] uses adaptive memory replay but focuses on memory budget, not KL-based function-space drift detection. Paper [24] "Detecting drifts in data streams using Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence" uses KL divergence for drift detection, but on raw data distributions, not on model outputs over an anchor set. Paper [18] "Function-Space Learning Rates" measures changes in neural network output functions (function-space), which is conceptually related to measuring function-space drift, but its purpose is setting learning rates, not triggering replay. No prior paper combines: (1) an anchor set, (2) KL divergence on model outputs (function space), and (3) using this as a signal to decide when to replay — as a replacement for parameter-space signals like FOREVER. This specific combination appears absent.

Paper [15] also evaluates on class incremental text classification benchmarks. These prior papers use the same evaluation design: multi-task sequential text classification benchmarks with standard accuracy/forgetting metrics. The 5-task variant is a parameter change, not a design change.

**DOMAIN: "LLM continual learning" (continual learning for large language models / NLP)**

Papers [14], [5], [15] all work in continual learning for text classification/NLP models. Paper [4] surveys continual learning broadly including NLP. This domain is clearly covered.
